scenario: 分层集成的内容审核系统在离线评测里报出 95% 的聚合 F1，团队想据此直接上线。
scenario_en: A tiered-ensemble moderation system reports 95% aggregate F1 offline, and the team wants to ship on that number.
q: 只报一个聚合 F1 会漏掉什么？为什么 L5+ 不这么收尾？
q_en: What does a single aggregate F1 hide, and why doesn't an L5+ engineer stop there?
why: 聚合 F1 把强子群和弱子群平均在一起，掩盖灾难性切片失败：可能英文垃圾抓 99%、印地语仇恨言论却漏 30%，某社区被超删 3×。L5+ 会沿政策相关维度拆解评测，并主动暴露公平性。
why_en: Aggregate F1 averages strong and weak subgroups together and masks catastrophic slice failures, so L5+ decomposes evaluation along policy-relevant dimensions and surfaces fairness proactively.
diagram:
flowchart TD I["分层审核系统"] --> A["聚合 F1 95%
看起来达标"] A -.掩盖.-> S1["英文垃圾 recall 99%"] A -.掩盖.-> S2["印地语仇恨 recall 70%
漏 30%"] A -.掩盖.-> S3["某社区 FPR 3×
被超删"]
options: 聚合 F1 过 95% 就代表各语言、各社区一致达标，把分类阈值再统一调高就能顺带补掉剩余漏检
应把单一 F1 换成 accuracy 当总指标，accuracy 天然把各子群的正负样本比例算进去、可替代切片评测
聚合 F1 掩盖切片灾难——英文垃圾抓 99% 却漏 30% 印地语仇恨、某社区被超删 3×；L5+ 沿政策维度拆解并主动暴露公平性
95% 里剩下的 5% 基本是标注噪声，按语言或社区再细分只会放大噪声、得不到有意义的结论
options_en: Passing 95% F1 means every language and community is uniformly fine; just raise the shared threshold to mop up any leftover misses.
Swap the single F1 for accuracy as the top metric — accuracy already accounts for each subgroup's class balance and can replace slice evaluation.
Aggregate F1 hides slice disasters — catching 99% of English spam but missing 30% of Hindi hate speech, over-removing one community 3x; L5+ decomposes by policy dimension and surfaces fairness.
The remaining 5% is mostly label noise, so slicing further by language or community only amplifies noise and yields nothing meaningful.
optionExplanations: 一个统一阈值救不了弱语言子群，反而会在强子群上过度删除；一致的聚合分不等于一致的子群表现。
accuracy 在类别极不平衡的审核里更容易被多数类主导，同样是单一聚合数，照样掩盖弱切片。
对；平均值把强弱子群糊在一起，必须按语言/社区/格式等政策维度拆开看，才能发现并主动修复不公平。
把弱子群的系统性漏检当噪声正是问题所在——那是真实伤害，用置信区间就能把它和采样噪声区分开。
optionExplanations_en: A single shared threshold can't rescue a weak language subgroup and would over-remove on strong ones; a uniform aggregate score is not uniform subgroup performance.
In heavily imbalanced moderation accuracy is dominated by the majority class; it is still one aggregate number that masks weak slices.
Correct — the average blends strong and weak subgroups, so you must slice by policy dimensions like language and community to find and fix inequity.
Treating a weak subgroup's systematic misses as noise is the bug — that is real harm, and confidence intervals separate it from sampling noise.

termDefinitions.meaning: 精确率和召回率的调和平均，单个数值衡量分类器综合表现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, a single number summarizing classifier performance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把所有样本混在一起算的单一 F1，会把子群差异平均掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Aggregate F1 is a single F1 computed over all samples pooled together, which averages away subgroup differences.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个维度(如语言、社区)切出的子群，用来单独评测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slice is a subgroup carved out along a dimension such as language or community, evaluated on its own.

scenario: 面试官问：把审核系统从「平均能用」推到「公平可用」，你会主动提出哪几支柱的评测？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks which evaluation pillars you'd proactively propose to move moderation from 'works on average' to 'works equitably'.
q: L5+ 审核评测的四支柱是哪些？(多选)
q_en: Which are the four pillars of L5+ moderation evaluation? (multiple)
why: 四支柱：成本敏感的按类别阈值、切片评测、反事实公平测试、把复审队列当 learning-to-rank。它们各自补一个「平均分看不见」的漏洞，应在被问公平性之前就主动提。
why_en: The four pillars are cost-sensitive per-category thresholds, slice-based evaluation, counterfactual fairness testing, and learning-to-rank queue prioritization, proposed before being asked.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  E["公平可用的审核评测"] --> P1["1 成本敏感阈值"]
  E --> P2["2 切片评测"]
  E --> P3["3 反事实公平"]
  E --> P4["4 LTR 复审队列"]
options: 按政策代价比给每个违规类别单独定阈值(成本敏感)
沿语言/社区/格式/作者人群切片独立算 P/R/F1/FPR
对个体做反事实公平测试并持续离线跑
把人工复审队列当作独立的 learning-to-rank 系统排优先级
options_en: Set each violation category its own threshold from a policy cost ratio (cost-sensitive).
Slice by language/community/format/author demographic and compute P/R/F1/FPR independently.
Run counterfactual fairness tests at the individual level, continuously offline.
Frame the human review queue as its own learning-to-rank system for prioritization.
optionExplanations: 对；FP 与 FN 代价悬殊，每类用自己的代价比选阈值，是支柱一。
对；只看聚合会掩盖弱子群，按维度切片独立评测是支柱二。
对；群体公平之外还要问「换个身份同一条内容会不会改判」，是支柱三。
对；每天上百万条升级/申诉，把排队当 LTR 最大化每人工时的伤害削减，是支柱四。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — FP and FN carry very different costs, so each category picks its threshold from its own ratio; pillar one.
Correct — aggregates hide weak subgroups, so slicing and evaluating independently is pillar two.
Correct — beyond group fairness you ask whether the same content flips decision under a swapped identity; pillar three.
Correct — millions of escalations/appeals a day, so treating the queue as LTR to maximize harm reduction per reviewer-hour is pillar four.

termDefinitions.fullName: Precision / Recall / F1 / False Positive Rate
termDefinitions.meaning: 精确率、召回率、F1、假阳率——审核里每个子群都要单独算的四个指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision, recall, F1 score, and false positive rate — the four metrics computed per subgroup in moderation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用机器学习给一批候选排序的技术，这里用来给复审队列排优先级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learning-to-Rank (LTR) is a machine-learning approach that orders a set of candidates, here used to prioritize the review queue.

scenario: 同一个审核系统要同时处理儿童安全和垃圾信息，两类的漏检代价天差地别(漏儿童安全=极端法律/人身伤害，漏删垃圾=轻微烦扰)。
scenario_en: One system moderates both child safety and spam, where a miss costs wildly different (missed child safety = extreme legal/human harm; missed spam = mild annoyance).
q: 阈值应该怎么设？
q_en: How should thresholds be set across these categories?
why: 给每个违规类别一条自己的阈值，从该类别的政策代价比(FN:FP)推出来：儿童安全代价比高就压低阈值最大化召回，垃圾信息代价比低就走平衡阈值。用一个全局阈值等于假设所有错误代价相同。
why_en: Give each violation category its own threshold derived from its policy cost ratio, so child safety maximizes recall while spam stays balanced.
tradeoff: 按类别代价比各自定阈值(对齐真实伤害) vs 单一全局阈值(假设错误代价都相同)
options: 给每个违规类别单独一条阈值，从该类别的政策代价比(FN:FP)推出：儿童安全压低阈值最大化召回、垃圾走平衡
所有类别共用一条阈值，取各类最优阈值的平均，简单统一、便于运维和 A/B 对比
所有类别都把阈值压到最低、一律最大化召回，宁可错删也绝不漏检，覆盖所有伤害
所有类别都把阈值提到最高、只在极高置信时才删，最大化精确率、把误删降到最低
options_en: Give each category its own threshold from its policy cost ratio (FN:FP): child safety lowers the threshold to maximize recall, spam stays balanced.
Share one threshold across categories, taking the average of each category's optimum, for simplicity and easier A/B comparison.
Push every category's threshold to the minimum and maximize recall across the board — better to over-remove than ever miss, covering all harm.
Push every category's threshold to the maximum and remove only at very high confidence, maximizing precision to keep wrongful removals minimal.
whenOtherWins: 若某个新品类还没标定政策代价比、样本也太少，可先临时套一个保守全局阈值兜底，等切片数据够了再拆成按类阈值。
optionExplanations: 对；漏儿童安全和漏垃圾代价差 50 倍，必须让代价比驱动各自阈值，才能把召回资源花在真正致命的类别上。
取平均会同时坑两头：儿童安全召回不够、垃圾又被过度删除，正是不同代价不能共用阈值的原因。
全局最大化召回会让垃圾类 FPR 爆炸、大量误删普通内容，把轻微烦扰问题升级成大规模冤删。
全局最大化精确率会让儿童安全大量漏检——这是代价 100:1 的类别，绝不能为了省误删而放过。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — missing child safety versus missing spam differ ~50x, so the cost ratio must drive each threshold to spend recall where harm is lethal.
Averaging hurts both ends: child safety recall falls short while spam gets over-removed — exactly why different costs can't share a threshold.
Global max-recall blows up spam FPR and mass-removes benign content, escalating a mild-annoyance problem into large-scale wrongful takedowns.
Global max-precision lets child safety leak badly — a 100:1 category you must never trade away to save on wrongful removals.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏检：一条真实违规内容被判为合规、没被删。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative is a truly violating item wrongly judged compliant and left up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 误删：一条合规内容被判为违规、被删掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive is a compliant item wrongly judged violating and removed.

termDefinitions.term: policy cost ratio / 政策代价比
termDefinitions.meaning: 某违规类别里 FN 相对 FP 的伤害倍数(如 100:1)，用来推阈值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The policy cost ratio is how much more a false negative harms than a false positive in a category (e.g. 100:1), used to set the threshold.

scenario: 把「不同错误代价不同」写成一个可优化的阈值选择目标。
scenario_en: Turn 'different errors cost differently' into an optimizable threshold-selection objective.
q: 补全成本敏感阈值的加权代价目标函数：
q_en: Complete the cost-sensitive weighted-cost objective:
text: 每个违规类别单独选阈值 θ，最小化总加权代价 min_θ Σ_i [ c_FN·{{FN}}_i(θ) + c_FP·{{FP}}_i(θ) ]；权重 c_FN、c_FP 来自该类别的政策代价比，比值越高越应偏向最大化{{召回}}。
text_en: Each category picks its own threshold to minimize weighted cost min over theta of sum c_FN times {{FN}} plus c_FP times {{FP}}; the weights come from that category's policy cost ratio, and a higher ratio favors maximizing {{recall}}.
why: 这不是从公式推出的固定数，而是把「漏检 vs 误删的相对代价」编码进目标：c_FN、c_FP 由政策代价比给定，θ 扫过阈值取总代价最低点。它的下游用途是为每个 classifier head 各选一条阈值。
why_en: The weights encode the miss-versus-wrongful-removal cost from the policy ratio, and sweeping theta to the minimum picks each classifier head's threshold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏检和误删各自的代价权重，来自违规类别的政策代价比。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: c_FN and c_FP are the cost weights for a miss and a wrongful removal, taken from the category's policy cost ratio.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分类器置信度高于它才判违规;调 θ 就是在召回和精确率间移动。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The threshold theta is the confidence cutoff above which an item is judged violating; tuning it trades recall against precision.

scenario: 审核政策给出各违规类别的代价比：儿童安全 100:1、仇恨言论 10:1、裸露 8:1、暴力 5:1、垃圾 2:1(FN:FP)。
scenario_en: Policy gives cost ratios (FN:FP): child safety 100:1, hate speech 10:1, nudity 8:1, violence 5:1, spam 2:1.
q: 这些代价比对阈值策略意味着什么？
q_en: What do these cost ratios imply for threshold strategy?
why: 代价比越高，漏检越致命，就越要压低阈值、最大化召回并留宽升级带；比值越接近 1(如垃圾 2:1)越走平衡阈值。这是一张政策输入表，不是模型算出来的，用来把每类阈值定向。
why_en: A higher ratio means a miss is more lethal, so lower the threshold to maximize recall, while a near-balanced ratio like spam 2:1 stays balanced.
options: 比值越高越该提高阈值、收紧删除，因为高代价类别更怕误删、要优先保护正常内容
所有类别代价比其实都应视为 1:1，表格只是示意，真正上线时统一用平衡阈值最稳妥
垃圾 2:1 该最大化召回、儿童安全 100:1 走平衡，代价越低越要激进删除以清干净
比值越高(如儿童安全 100:1)越压低阈值、最大化召回并留宽升级带；比值接近 1(垃圾 2:1)走平衡阈值
options_en: The higher the ratio the higher the threshold and the tighter the removal, since high-cost categories fear wrongful removal most.
All ratios should really be treated as 1:1; the table is illustrative, and in production a single balanced threshold is safest.
Spam 2:1 should maximize recall while child safety 100:1 stays balanced — lower cost means remove more aggressively to keep things clean.
A higher ratio (child safety 100:1) lowers the threshold, maximizes recall, and keeps a wide escalation band; a near-1 ratio (spam 2:1) stays balanced.
optionExplanations: 方向反了：高代价比怕的是漏检(FN)不是误删，应压低阈值多抓，而不是收紧。
把代价比抹平就丢掉了这套方法的全部价值——不同伤害本就该用不同阈值区别对待。
对应关系整个颠倒：100:1 才该最大化召回，2:1 才走平衡，这里说反了。
对；FN:FP 越大代表漏检伤害越大，用低阈值+宽升级带把召回拉满,平衡类保持中性阈值。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: a high ratio fears the miss (FN), not the wrongful removal, so lower the threshold to catch more, not tighten it.
Flattening the ratios throws away the whole method — different harms should be treated with different thresholds.
The mapping is inverted: 100:1 should maximize recall and 2:1 stays balanced, stated the wrong way round.
Correct — a larger FN:FP means a miss hurts more, so a low threshold plus a wide escalation band maxes recall while balanced categories stay neutral.

termDefinitions.meaning: 介于「明显合规」和「明显违规」之间、送人工复审的置信度区间;儿童安全留得宽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The escalation band is the confidence range between clearly-fine and clearly-violating that gets routed to human review, kept wide for child safety.

scenario: 一个多头分类器同时输出儿童安全、仇恨、裸露、暴力、垃圾等多个违规分数,每类代价比不同。
scenario_en: A multi-head classifier outputs scores for child safety, hate, nudity, violence, spam simultaneously, each with a different cost ratio.
q: 系统运行期怎么应用这些按类阈值？
q_en: How does the system apply these per-category thresholds at runtime?
why: 系统同时跑多条阈值,每个 classifier head 一条自己的阈值,同一条内容的每个违规维度各自判定。不是一条全局阈值卡所有维度,否则代价差异就白定了。
why_en: The system runs multiple thresholds simultaneously, one per classifier head, so each violation dimension is judged against its own cutoff.
options: 取所有类别阈值里最严的那条,对每条内容统一套用,保证最危险类别绝不漏检
同时运行多条阈值,每个 classifier head 一条自己的阈值,内容的每个违规维度各自判定
按内容先猜属于哪一类,只用那一类的阈值判一次,省掉多头计算、降低延迟
对每条内容轮流套用五条阈值、投票取多数,多数判违规才删,降低单头误判
options_en: Take the strictest of all category thresholds and apply it uniformly to every item, guaranteeing the most dangerous category never leaks.
Run multiple thresholds simultaneously, one per classifier head, so each violation dimension of an item is judged against its own cutoff.
Guess each item's single category first and apply only that category's threshold once, saving multi-head compute and latency.
Apply all five thresholds to each item in turn and majority-vote — remove only if most flag it — to reduce single-head misjudgment.
optionExplanations: 统一用最严阈值会让低代价类别(垃圾)FPR 爆炸、大量误删,浪费了按类定制的意义。
对;多头各判各的,一条内容可以同时在仇恨维度过阈值、在裸露维度不过,互不干扰。
先猜单一类别会漏掉同时踩多条红线的内容,也把误分类风险前置到一个脆弱的路由步骤。
投票把不同代价的维度混为一谈,儿童安全一票就该升级,不能被其它维度的「否」淹没。
optionExplanations_en: One strictest threshold blows up FPR on low-cost categories like spam and mass-removes, wasting the per-category customization.
Correct — each head judges independently, so an item can pass the hate threshold yet not the nudity one, with no cross-interference.
Guessing a single category misses content crossing several red lines and front-loads misclassification risk into a brittle router.
Voting conflates dimensions of different cost; one child-safety hit should escalate and must not be outvoted by other dimensions' 'no'.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多头模型里负责一个违规类别输出分数的分支,每个头配自己的阈值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A classifier head is a branch of a multi-head model that outputs a score for one violation category, each with its own threshold.

scenario: 分类器在 0.7 这个分数段输出置信度,但离线检查发现该段真实正例率其实只有 0.5。
scenario_en: The classifier outputs 0.7 confidence at a score band, but offline checks show the true positive rate there is only 0.5.
q: 这对按分数调阈值意味着什么?
q_en: What does this mean for tuning thresholds by score?
why: 置信度没校准:分数不等于真实正例率,按 0.7 设阈值实际抓到的准确度只有 0.5,阈值和代价比的映射就失真了。必须先做校准(如温度缩放/Platt/isotonic)让分数对齐真实概率,阈值调优才可靠。
why_en: Miscalibrated scores mean the threshold no longer maps to real accuracy, so you must calibrate before cost-based tuning is trustworthy.
options: 问题不大,只要把阈值从 0.7 挪到 0.5 补偿一下,数值对齐后就等于校准好了,无需额外处理
分数偏高说明模型太保守,应整体调低所有阈值、多删一些,自然把 recall 补回来即可
置信度未校准:0.7 处真实正例率只有 0.5,阈值与代价比的映射失真,必须先做校准(温度缩放等)再调阈值
只要模型 AUC 够高就无所谓校准,排序对了阈值随便设,校准只影响可解释性不影响删除决策
options_en: Not a big deal — just shift the threshold from 0.7 to 0.5 to compensate; once the numbers line up it's effectively calibrated, no extra work needed.
A high score means the model is too conservative, so lower all thresholds and remove more to naturally recover recall.
The confidence is uncalibrated: at 0.7 the true positive rate is only 0.5, so the threshold-to-cost mapping is distorted and you must calibrate (temperature scaling, etc.) before tuning.
As long as AUC is high, calibration doesn't matter — if the ranking is right you can set the threshold anywhere; calibration only affects interpretability, not removal decisions.
optionExplanations: 单点平移救不了整条曲线:其它分数段偏差不同,挪一个点只是治标,映射整体还是错的。
无根据地整体降阈值会把 FPR 一起抬高,而且没解决「分数不代表概率」这个根因。
对;成本敏感阈值假设分数=概率,校准失真会让代价比推出的阈值完全错位,先校准是前提。
AUC 只看排序、不看概率是否准;成本敏感阈值恰恰依赖概率对齐,所以校准在这里是刚需。
optionExplanations_en: Shifting one point can't fix the whole curve — other bands are off by different amounts, so the mapping stays wrong.
Blindly lowering all thresholds raises FPR too and never fixes the root cause that the score isn't a probability.
Correct — cost-sensitive thresholds assume score equals probability, so miscalibration misplaces the cost-derived threshold; calibrate first.
AUC only judges ranking, not whether probabilities are accurate; cost-sensitive thresholds depend on calibrated probabilities, so calibration is required here.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让模型输出的置信度等于真实正例率:输出 0.7 的样本里应有约 70% 真为正。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration makes the model's confidence equal the true positive rate, so items scored 0.7 are truly positive about 70% of the time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实正例中被正确判为正的比例,等价于召回率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: True positive rate is the fraction of actual positives correctly flagged, equivalent to recall.

scenario: 儿童安全类的政策代价比是 100:1(漏一条的法律与人身伤害极高,误删一条只是轻微烦扰)。
scenario_en: Child safety carries a 100:1 cost ratio — a miss is extreme legal/human harm, a wrongful removal is a mild annoyance.
q: 该怎么给儿童安全类定阈值?
q_en: How should you set the child-safety threshold?
why: 代价比 100:1 意味着宁可多误删也绝不能漏,应压低阈值最大化召回,并留一条宽升级带把边界样本送人工。代价是精确率下降、误删增多,但相对漏检的伤害完全可接受。
why_en: At 100:1 you maximize recall with a low threshold and a wide escalation band, accepting more wrongful removals because a miss is catastrophic.
tradeoff: 低阈值最大化召回(几乎不漏,但误删多) vs 高阈值保精确率(误删少,但漏检风险致命)
options: 提高阈值、追求高精确率,只在极高置信时才删,把误删控制到最低以免打扰正常用户
压低阈值、最大化召回,并留宽升级带把边界样本送人工,代价是误删增多但绝不漏检
沿用垃圾类同一条平衡阈值,保持全系统一致,方便运维和跨类对比指标
完全交给人工、不设自动阈值,任何疑似都排队等人看,靠人力保证零漏检
options_en: Raise the threshold for high precision, removing only at very high confidence to keep wrongful removals minimal and avoid bothering normal users.
Lower the threshold to maximize recall and keep a wide escalation band sending borderline items to humans, accepting more wrongful removals but never missing.
Reuse the same balanced threshold as spam for system-wide consistency and easier ops and cross-category metric comparison.
Skip automated thresholds entirely and route every suspected item to a human queue, relying on manpower for zero misses.
whenOtherWins: 当误删本身会造成严重次生伤害(如误删合法新闻/证据、压制某群体表达)时,即便高代价类别也要收敛升级带、加人工前置复核,而不是无脑最大化召回。
optionExplanations: 追精确率会放大漏检,而 100:1 的类别漏一条的代价远超误删一堆,方向完全相反。
对;高代价比就该把召回拉满,用宽升级带兜住边界样本,误删的轻微代价换掉致命漏检。
共用平衡阈值等于假设儿童安全和垃圾代价一样,直接违背 100:1 的政策前提。
纯人工扛不住规模(每天百万级),延迟高、必然积压,反而制造大量漏检窗口。
optionExplanations_en: Chasing precision amplifies misses, but in a 100:1 category one miss dwarfs many wrongful removals — the opposite direction.
Correct — a high cost ratio maxes recall with a wide escalation band for borderline items, trading mild wrongful removals for avoiding a lethal miss.
A shared balanced threshold assumes child safety costs the same as spam, directly violating the 100:1 premise.
Pure human review can't handle millions/day; it lags and backlogs, opening large windows of misses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实违规中被系统抓到的比例;最大化召回=尽量不漏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of true violations the system catches; maximizing recall means missing as few as possible.

scenario: 系统聚合 F1 达标,但你怀疑不同语言、社区的表现差异很大,想量化公平性。
scenario_en: Aggregate F1 looks fine, but you suspect large gaps across languages and communities and want to quantify fairness.
q: 评测应该怎么组织?
q_en: How should you organize the evaluation?
why: 沿政策相关维度切片,对每个子群独立算 precision/recall/F1/FPR,再设一个最大差异阈值(如任一切片的 FPR 不超过全局均值 2×)。只看聚合会把弱子群平均掉,切片才能定位并约束不公平。
why_en: Slice by policy dimensions and compute precision/recall/F1/FPR independently per subgroup, then cap disparity so no slice's FPR exceeds twice the global average.
tradeoff: 按子群独立算指标+设差异上限(能定位不公平) vs 只看聚合(弱子群被平均掩盖)
diagram:
flowchart TD D["评测集"] --> L1["英文切片
P/R/F1/FPR"] D --> L2["印地语切片
P/R/F1/FPR"] D --> L3["斯瓦希里语切片
P/R/F1/FPR"] L1 & L2 & L3 --> C["最大差异阈值
FPR 不超全局均值 2×"]
options: 继续用聚合 F1,只要总分够高就代表各子群整体健康,细分维度会稀释统计功效
只报聚合 F1 加一个总体 FPR,两个全局数就够覆盖公平性,再细分是过度工程
把所有语言样本混合后重训模型再看总分,数据混得越匀公平性越好,不需要分子群评测
沿语言/社区等维度切片,对每个子群独立算 P/R/F1/FPR,并设最大差异阈值(如 FPR 不超全局均值 2×)
options_en: Keep using aggregate F1 — a high total means each subgroup is healthy overall, and slicing just dilutes statistical power.
Report aggregate F1 plus one overall FPR; two global numbers cover fairness, and finer slicing is over-engineering.
Mix all languages and retrain, then read the total score — the more evenly mixed the data the fairer it is, no per-subgroup eval needed.
Slice by language/community and compute P/R/F1/FPR independently per subgroup, plus a max disparity cap (e.g. FPR not over 2x the global average).
whenOtherWins: 当某切片样本极少(如 50 条)、点估计噪声太大时,不能直接拿它和全局比,要先用置信区间判断差异是否真实,再决定是否触发差异阈值。
optionExplanations: 聚合分高恰恰能掩盖弱子群,这正是切片评测要解决的盲区,不是稀释功效。
两个全局数无法暴露「印地语 FPR 是英文 3 倍」这类差异,公平性必须按子群量化。
混合重训改的是模型,不是评测口径;不分子群看,仍然不知道哪个群体被系统性坑了。
对;独立指标+差异上限把公平性变成可监控、可约束的量,能精确定位并限制被超删/漏检的子群。
optionExplanations_en: A high aggregate is exactly what hides weak subgroups — the blind spot slice eval fixes, not a power dilution.
Two global numbers can't reveal 'Hindi FPR is 3x English'; fairness must be quantified per subgroup.
Retraining changes the model, not the measurement; without slicing you still don't know which group is systematically harmed.
Correct — independent metrics plus a disparity cap make fairness monitorable and boundable, pinpointing and limiting over-removed or missed subgroups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把评测集按维度切成子群,对每个子群单独算指标,而不是只看总分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Slice-based evaluation splits the eval set into subgroups along a dimension and computes metrics per subgroup, not just overall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 合规内容中被误判为违规的比例,衡量对某群体的超删程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: False positive rate is the fraction of compliant content wrongly flagged, measuring how much a group is over-removed.

scenario: 你要设计切片评测,得先确定沿哪些维度切子群才能覆盖真实的公平性风险。
scenario_en: Designing slice evaluation, you must decide which axes to slice along to cover real fairness risks.
q: 切片评测常用哪些切分维度?(多选)
q_en: Which axes are commonly used to slice moderation evaluation? (multiple)
why: 四类政策相关切片维度:语言(英/西/印地/阿拉伯/斯瓦希里)、社区类型(游戏/政治/宗教)、内容格式(文本/图文/短视频/直播)、作者人群(地区/自报,合规前提下)。这些是不公平最常沿之分布的轴。
why_en: Slice by language, community type, content format, and author demographic — the axes along which moderation inequity most often falls.
options: 语言(英文/西班牙语/印地语/阿拉伯语/斯瓦希里语)
社区类型(游戏/政治/宗教)
内容格式(纯文本/图文/短视频/直播)
作者人群(地区/自报人口属性,在隐私合规前提下)
options_en: Language (English/Spanish/Hindi/Arabic/Swahili).
Community type (gaming/political/religious).
Content format (text/image+text/short video/live).
Author demographic (region/self-reported, where privacy-compliant).
optionExplanations: 对;低资源语言的训练数据和标注质量差,最容易出现召回塌陷,是首要切片轴。
对;政治/宗教社区的表达常被过度删除,社区维度能抓到这类群体级偏差。
对;直播/短视频的检测难度和延迟约束不同,格式维度暴露模态间的表现差。
对;作者人群维度直指人口层面的公平,但要在隐私合规前提下用自报/地区数据。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — low-resource languages have poor training data and labels and are most prone to recall collapse, the primary slice axis.
Correct — political/religious communities often get over-removed, and the community axis catches such group-level bias.
Correct — live/short video differ in detection difficulty and latency, so the format axis exposes cross-modal performance gaps.
Correct — the author-demographic axis targets population-level fairness, using self-reported/region data only where privacy-compliant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容作者的地区或自报人口属性,仅在隐私合规时用于公平性切片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Author demographic is the content author's region or self-reported attributes, used for fairness slicing only where privacy-compliant.

scenario: 团队要给切片评测定一个可执行的公平性红线,例如「任一切片的 FPR 不得超过全局均值的 2×」。
scenario_en: The team wants an actionable fairness line, e.g. 'no slice's FPR may exceed 2x the global average'.
q: 这个 2× 差异阈值是什么性质、约束了什么?
q_en: What kind of number is this 2x disparity threshold, and what does it constrain?
why: 2× 是一个团队设定的公平性目标(SLO 性质),不是公式推导出来的;它把「不公平」变成可监控的告警线——一旦某切片 FPR 超全局均值 2× 就触发调查或按切片调阈值。数值可按政策收紧或放宽。
why_en: The 2x cap is a chosen fairness target, not a derived constant, turning inequity into a monitorable alarm that triggers per-slice fixes when breached.
options: 它是团队设定的公平性目标(SLO 性质),把差异变成可监控告警线,超线就触发调查或按切片调阈值
它是从 FPR 分布用统计公式(如 2 倍标准差)推出的固定阈值,任何系统都必须用 2× 不可改
它是模型精度的硬上限,意思是全局 FPR 不能超过 50%,和子群差异无关
它是延迟指标,要求慢切片的处理时间不超过快切片 2×,与公平性无直接关系
options_en: It's a chosen fairness target (SLO-like) that turns disparity into a monitorable alarm; breaching it triggers investigation or per-slice threshold fixes.
It's a fixed threshold derived by a statistical formula (like 2 standard deviations) from the FPR distribution, mandatory as 2x for every system.
It's a hard cap on model accuracy meaning global FPR can't exceed 50%, unrelated to subgroup disparity.
It's a latency metric requiring slow slices to process within 2x of fast slices, not directly about fairness.
optionExplanations: 对;它是主动定的目标线,作用是把公平性从口号变成可告警、可整改的运营约束,阈值本身可调。
它不是统计公式的必然产物,2× 是政策选择,不同产品/法域可以定更严或更松。
它约束的是子群间 FPR 的相对差异,不是全局精度上限,50% 之说无依据。
它是关于误删公平的比率,不是延迟指标,把两者混淆了。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it's a deliberately set target line that turns fairness into an alertable, fixable operational constraint, and the value itself is tunable.
It's not an inevitable statistical output; 2x is a policy choice that different products or jurisdictions can tighten or loosen.
It constrains relative FPR disparity across subgroups, not a global accuracy cap; the 50% claim is baseless.
It's a fairness ratio on wrongful removals, not a latency metric — the two are conflated here.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许的最大子群间指标差(如 FPR 不超全局均值 2×),是公平性红线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A disparity threshold is the max allowed gap between subgroups, e.g. no slice's FPR over 2x the global average — the fairness red line.

termDefinitions.meaning: 团队自定的目标指标(不是推导值),用作监控与告警的基准线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a team-chosen target metric, not a derived value, used as the baseline for monitoring and alerting.

scenario: 斯瓦希里语切片只有 50 条评测样本,点估计召回率是 0.72,团队想据此判定该语言表现差、触发整改。
scenario_en: The Swahili slice has only 50 eval examples with a 0.72 recall point estimate, and the team wants to declare it underperforming.
q: 拿这个 0.72 直接下结论有什么问题?
q_en: What's wrong with concluding from that 0.72 directly?
why: 50 条样本的点估计噪声极大,0.72 的置信区间可能横跨 0.6~0.85,分不清是真实缺口还是采样噪声。要给小切片算置信区间,区间够窄且低于阈值才判定为真实不公平,否则先扩样本。
why_en: On 50 examples the point estimate is noisy, so use confidence intervals to tell a genuine gap from sampling noise before acting.
options: 没问题,0.72 已经低于全局,样本多少不影响结论,直接判定该语言不达标并整改即可
问题在于该切片样本太多导致过拟合,应随机丢弃一半样本再算,数字会更可信
50 条样本点估计噪声极大,应算置信区间区分真实缺口与采样噪声,区间够窄且低于阈值才判定不公平
问题在于召回率不适合小样本,换成 accuracy 就能消除小样本带来的不确定性
options_en: Nothing wrong — 0.72 is already below global, sample size doesn't affect the conclusion, so declare the language failing and fix it.
The problem is too many samples causing overfitting; randomly drop half and recompute for a more trustworthy number.
On 50 examples the point estimate is very noisy, so compute a confidence interval to separate a real gap from sampling noise, acting only if the interval is narrow and below threshold.
The problem is recall doesn't suit small samples; switch to accuracy to remove the small-sample uncertainty.
optionExplanations: 无视样本量会把随机波动当成系统性缺口,可能触发错误整改、甚至反向恶化其它切片。
丢样本只会让区间更宽、噪声更大,和「过拟合」无关,方向完全错。
对;小切片先看区间宽度,区间宽=证据不足要先扩样本,窄且低于阈值才算真实公平性问题。
换指标改变不了样本量小这个根因,accuracy 在小样本下同样噪声大,不解决问题。
optionExplanations_en: Ignoring sample size treats random fluctuation as a systematic gap, risking a wrong fix that could even worsen other slices.
Dropping samples only widens the interval and adds noise — unrelated to overfitting and the wrong direction.
Correct — for small slices check the interval width: wide means insufficient evidence, gather more; only a narrow interval below threshold is a real fairness issue.
Switching metrics doesn't fix the small-sample root cause; accuracy is just as noisy on 50 examples.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点估计上下的一段区间,表示真值大概率落在其中;样本越少区间越宽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A confidence interval is a range around a point estimate likely to contain the true value; fewer samples make it wider.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单个样本算出的单点数值(如 recall=0.72),不含不确定性信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A point estimate is a single computed value like recall 0.72, carrying no uncertainty information by itself.

scenario: 面试官质疑切片评测是不是「学术上好看、工业界不做」的理论。
scenario_en: The interviewer challenges whether slice evaluation is just academically nice but not done in industry.
q: 有什么证据说明切片评测是工业界的运营现实?
q_en: What shows slice evaluation is operational reality, not theory?
why: Meta、YouTube 会公开发布按语言的错误率透明度报告,这说明按子群拆解误差已是大平台的运营实践,不是纸上谈兵。面试里不待被问就主动提切片评测,能体现 L5/Staff 的公平性意识。
why_en: Meta and YouTube publish per-language error-rate transparency reports, proving slice evaluation is operational practice, not theory.
options: 没有真实证据,切片评测只是研究论文里的理想,大平台内部仍只看聚合 F1 上线
Meta、YouTube 公开发布按语言的错误率透明度报告,说明按子群拆误差是大平台的运营实践
证据是各平台都用同一个开源基准榜单打分,谁分高谁上线,与语言子群无关
证据是监管只要求报告总删除量,平台按总量披露即可,不涉及按语言的误差拆解
options_en: No real evidence — slice eval is a research-paper ideal, and big platforms still ship on aggregate F1 internally.
Meta and YouTube publish per-language error-rate transparency reports, showing per-subgroup error breakdown is operational practice at scale.
The evidence is that platforms all score on one shared open benchmark leaderboard and ship whoever ranks highest, unrelated to language subgroups.
The evidence is that regulators only require reporting total removal volume, so platforms disclose totals with no per-language error breakdown.
optionExplanations: 与事实相反:大平台确有按语言/地区的公开透明度报告,切片评测是既成实践。
对;公开的按语言错误率报告就是切片评测在工业界落地的直接证据。
开源榜单单分不等于按语言子群拆误差,和切片评测的运营现实不是一回事。
只报总量恰恰是要被切片评测取代的粗口径,透明度报告已细化到语言维度。
optionExplanations_en: The opposite of fact: big platforms do publish per-language/region transparency reports, so slice eval is established practice.
Correct — public per-language error-rate reports are direct evidence of slice evaluation deployed in industry.
A single leaderboard score isn't a per-language error breakdown and isn't the operational reality of slice eval.
Reporting only totals is the coarse metric slice eval replaces; transparency reports already break down by language.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平台定期公开的审核执行数据,含按语言/地区的错误率与删除量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transparency report is a platform's periodic public disclosure of moderation stats, including per-language/region error rates and removals.

scenario: 切片评测保证了群体级的误差均衡,但你还想确认单条内容不会因作者身份不同而被区别对待。
scenario_en: Slice eval ensures group-level error balance, but you also want to confirm a single item isn't treated differently by author identity.
q: 反事实公平在个体层面问的是什么?
q_en: What does counterfactual fairness ask at the individual level?
why: 反事实公平问:这条一模一样的内容,如果作者身份换成另一组,决策会不会变?它是个体级的检验,和切片评测的群体级均衡互补——群体均衡不代表每一条都被一致对待。
why_en: Counterfactual fairness asks whether the exact same content would get the same decision if the author's demographic were different — an individual-level check.
options: 问的是不同语言子群的平均 FPR 是否相等,本质就是切片评测换个名字
问的是模型总体准确率是否达到某个阈值,与作者身份无关
问的是训练集里各人群样本量是否平衡,数量均衡就算公平
问的是这条一模一样的内容若作者身份换成另一组、决策会不会变——个体级检验
options_en: Whether the average FPR is equal across language subgroups — essentially slice eval by another name.
Whether the model's overall accuracy meets some threshold, independent of author identity.
Whether the training set has balanced sample counts across demographics — equal counts means fair.
Whether this exact same content would get a different decision if the author's demographic were swapped — an individual-level test.
optionExplanations: 那是群体级切片评测;反事实公平是逐条内容做身份替换,粒度和问题都不同。
总体准确率完全不触及「同内容不同身份是否改判」这一反事实问题。
训练样本量平衡是数据侧措施,不等于对单条内容的决策不受身份影响。
对;反事实公平锁定同一内容、只改身份特征,看决策是否变,是个体级的公平检验。
optionExplanations_en: That's group-level slice eval; counterfactual fairness swaps identity per individual item — a different granularity and question.
Overall accuracy never touches the counterfactual question of whether the same content flips under a different identity.
Balanced training counts is a data-side measure, not proof that a single item's decision is identity-invariant.
Correct — counterfactual fairness holds the content fixed, swaps only identity features, and checks if the decision changes; an individual-level test.

termDefinitions.meaning: 个体级公平:同一内容仅改作者身份特征时,模型决策应保持不变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Counterfactual fairness is individual-level: swapping only the author's identity features on the same content should not change the model's decision.

q: 把反事实公平测试的协议排成正确顺序:
q_en: Order the counterfactual fairness testing protocol correctly:
steps: 测量违规分变化是否超过阈值 epsilon,超过即判为反事实不公平
选一段内容,锁定除身份相关特征外的所有其它因素不变
把身份相关特征替换成另一组(如 AAVE→标准美式英语、Muhammad→John)
把原始与替换后的两份内容分别送进同一个模型打分
why: 协议是:固定其它一切→只替换身份特征→同一模型对两份各打分→比较分差是否超 epsilon。分差超阈值说明决策被身份驱动,就是反事实不公平。
why_en: Hold everything else fixed, swap only identity features, score both with the same model, and flag if the score gap exceeds epsilon.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["锁定其它因素不变"] --> B["替换身份特征
AAVE→标准英语"] B --> C["同一模型分别打分"] C --> D["分差是否超 epsilon"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 非裔美国人白话英语,一种方言;模型常错误地把它判为更毒。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AAVE (African American Vernacular English) is a dialect that models often wrongly flag as more toxic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许的最大分数变化;身份替换后分差超过它即判为不公平。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Epsilon is the max allowed score change; a gap larger than it after an identity swap is flagged as unfair.

termDefinitions.term: identity-correlated feature / 身份相关特征
termDefinitions.meaning: 与作者人群相关的信号,如方言标记、宗教名字,反事实测试专门替换它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Identity-correlated features are signals tied to author demographic, like dialect markers or religious names, which counterfactual testing swaps.

scenario: 研究发现:用人工标注的毒性数据训练的模型,会不成比例地把 AAVE(非裔白话英语)判为有毒。
scenario_en: Research shows models trained on human-labeled toxicity data disproportionately flag AAVE as toxic.
q: 这种偏差主要来自哪里、怎么理解?
q_en: Where does this bias mainly come from and how should you read it?
why: 偏差主要源自训练标签本身:标注者带着自身偏见把 AAVE 更多标为有毒,模型只是忠实地学到了这份被污染的标签。所以根因不在模型结构,而在数据标注环节,得从标注/去偏两侧治理。
why_en: The bias originates in the training labels — annotators' biases baked into the data, which the model faithfully learns.
options: 主要来自训练标签:标注者偏见把 AAVE 更多标为有毒,模型忠实学到这份被污染的标签
主要来自模型太小、容量不足,换更大的模型就能自动消除对 AAVE 的误判
主要来自推理时的随机性,固定随机种子、关掉采样温度就能让 AAVE 判定回归正常
主要来自 AAVE 语料在训练集里过多,做下采样减少其占比即可去掉这种偏差
options_en: Mainly the training labels — annotators' biases flag AAVE as toxic more often, and the model faithfully learns those tainted labels.
Mainly the model being too small; a larger model would automatically remove the AAVE misjudgment.
Mainly inference randomness; fixing the seed and turning off sampling temperature restores normal AAVE judgments.
Mainly too much AAVE data in training; downsampling it to a smaller share removes the bias.
optionExplanations: 对;标签是监督信号的源头,标注偏见进了标签,模型学得越好偏差越牢,根治要从标注和去偏入手。
加大模型只会更精确地拟合有偏标签,容量不是根因,反而可能放大偏差。
这是系统性的标签偏差,不是随机噪声,固定种子改变不了学到的有偏决策边界。
问题是标签把 AAVE 错标为毒,不是样本量多少;单纯下采样不纠正错误标签,偏差仍在。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — labels are the supervision source, so annotator bias in the labels is learned ever more firmly; the fix starts at labeling and debiasing.
A bigger model just fits the biased labels more precisely; capacity isn't the cause and may amplify the bias.
This is systematic label bias, not random noise; fixing the seed doesn't change the biased decision boundary learned.
The issue is labels wrongly marking AAVE toxic, not sample count; downsampling alone doesn't correct wrong labels, so the bias persists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练标签本身带有系统性偏见,模型会忠实地把它学进决策里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Label bias is systematic prejudice in the training labels themselves, which the model faithfully learns into its decisions.

scenario: 确认了模型对 AAVE 存在毒性误判后,你要在训练/上线各环节部署去偏手段。
scenario_en: Having confirmed AAVE toxicity misjudgment, you deploy debiasing across training and deployment.
q: 反事实公平的常用缓解手段有哪些?(多选)
q_en: Which are common mitigations for counterfactual fairness? (multiple)
why: 三类:对抗去偏(惩罚能预测敏感属性的表示)、反事实数据增强(训练时要求原始/替换对给出相等预测)、事后阈值调整(按切片调阈值以拉平 FPR)。分别作用在表示、数据、决策三层。
why_en: Adversarial debiasing, counterfactual data augmentation, and post-hoc threshold adjustment attack bias at the representation, data, and decision layers.
options: 对抗去偏:惩罚那些能从中预测出敏感属性的内部表示
反事实数据增强:训练时要求原始与身份替换后的样本对给出相等预测
事后阈值调整:按切片分别调阈值以拉平各子群的 FPR
直接删掉所有含身份词的样本,不含身份词模型就学不到偏差
options_en: Adversarial debiasing: penalize internal representations from which the sensitive attribute can be predicted.
Counterfactual data augmentation: train for equal predictions on original/identity-swapped pairs.
Post-hoc threshold adjustment: set per-slice thresholds to equalize FPR across subgroups.
Just delete all samples containing identity terms — without identity words the model can't learn bias.
optionExplanations: 对;对抗去偏在表示层动手,让编码器学不出能泄露敏感属性的表示。
对;数据增强在数据层动手,用成对约束逼模型对身份替换保持不变。
对;事后阈值调整在决策层动手,不改模型、按切片调阈值把 FPR 拉齐。
错;删身份词会丢掉真实的反穆斯林等仇恨语境,还挡不住模型从相关词学到代理特征。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — adversarial debiasing acts at the representation layer so the encoder can't encode the sensitive attribute.
Correct — augmentation acts at the data layer, forcing invariance to identity swaps via paired constraints.
Correct — post-hoc adjustment acts at the decision layer, equalizing FPR by per-slice thresholds without touching the model.
Wrong — deleting identity terms loses real anti-Muslim hate context and doesn't stop the model learning proxy features from correlated words.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加一个对手网络去预测敏感属性,惩罚主模型让其表示预测不出该属性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adversarial debiasing adds an adversary predicting the sensitive attribute and penalizes the main model so its representation can't.

termDefinitions.term: counterfactual data augmentation / 反事实数据增强
termDefinitions.meaning: 生成身份替换的样本对,训练模型对两者输出相等预测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Counterfactual data augmentation creates identity-swapped sample pairs and trains the model for equal predictions on both.

termDefinitions.term: post-hoc threshold adjustment / 事后阈值调整
termDefinitions.meaning: 训练后按子群分别设阈值,以拉平各子群的假阳率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Post-hoc threshold adjustment sets per-subgroup thresholds after training to equalize false positive rates.

scenario: 毒性模型的内部表示里泄露了作者方言(能从中预测出是不是 AAVE),导致同义内容因方言不同而改判。你想在表示层根治。
scenario_en: The toxicity model's representation leaks author dialect (AAVE is predictable from it), flipping decisions on equivalent content; you want a representation-layer fix.
q: 该用哪种缓解手段?
q_en: Which mitigation fits?
why: 对抗去偏:接一个对手网络专门从表示里预测敏感属性,主模型被惩罚到「让对手预测不出方言」,从而在表示层剥离身份信号。它直击「表示泄露身份」这个根因,而不是只在决策端补救。
why_en: Adversarial debiasing penalizes the representation whenever an adversary can predict the sensitive attribute, stripping identity signal at the source.
tradeoff: 对抗去偏(表示层剥离身份,治本但可能伤召回) vs 事后阈值(决策层拉平 FPR,不改表示、治标)
options: 事后阈值调整:训练完不动模型,只按方言切片各调一条阈值把 FPR 拉平
反事实数据增强:多造方言替换的样本对喂进去,靠数据量稀释偏差
对抗去偏:用对手网络从表示里预测方言,惩罚主模型使其表示预测不出身份属性
直接给模型加一个「忽略方言」的系统提示,让它自己声明不看方言即可
options_en: Post-hoc threshold adjustment: leave the model, set a separate threshold per dialect slice to equalize FPR.
Counterfactual data augmentation: add more dialect-swapped pairs to dilute the bias by data volume.
Adversarial debiasing: use an adversary predicting dialect from the representation and penalize the main model so its representation can't reveal the identity attribute.
Just add a system prompt telling the model to 'ignore dialect' so it declares it won't look at dialect.
whenOtherWins: 如果不想重训模型、只需快速把上线后的子群 FPR 差异压到合规线内,事后阈值调整更省事;但它不改表示,身份信号仍留在模型里。
optionExplanations: 事后阈值是决策层补救、不动表示,题目要的是在表示层根治泄露,不匹配。
数据增强有用,但它靠成对约束而非「稀释」,且不像对抗法直接盯着表示是否泄露身份。
对;题目锁定「表示泄露方言」这一根因,对抗去偏正是惩罚可预测敏感属性的表示,直击此处。
系统提示不改变已学到的有偏表示,模型仍从内部特征读出方言,声明无效。
optionExplanations_en: Post-hoc thresholds patch the decision layer without touching the representation; the task wants a representation-layer cure, so it doesn't fit.
Augmentation helps but works via paired constraints, not 'dilution', and doesn't directly target whether the representation leaks identity.
Correct — the task pins the root cause 'representation leaks dialect', and adversarial debiasing penalizes exactly a representation that predicts the sensitive attribute.
A system prompt doesn't change the already-learned biased representation; the model still reads dialect from internal features, so the declaration is empty.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不应影响决策的身份属性,如种族、方言、宗教。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sensitive attribute is an identity property that shouldn't affect decisions, such as race, dialect, or religion.

scenario: 为了消除对宗教相关词的偏差,团队对含宗教词的内容做了激进去偏,结果发现真实的反穆斯林仇恨言论开始被漏检。
scenario_en: To remove bias on religious terms, aggressive debiasing was applied, and real anti-Muslim hate speech started slipping through.
q: 这暴露了去偏的什么张力?
q_en: What tension in debiasing does this expose?
why: 去偏和召回之间有张力:过度去偏会把「宗教词」整体钝化,连带压低对该保护群体内真实违规的召回(过度去偏宗教词→漏掉真实反穆斯林仇恨)。所以去偏强度要校准,不能一味求「不敏感」。
why_en: Aggressive debiasing can dull genuine violation signals within the protected group, so over-debiasing religious terms misses real anti-Muslim hate.
tradeoff: 激进去偏(更公平但漏检保护群体内真实违规) vs 保守去偏(召回稳但可能残留偏差)
options: 说明去偏永远有害,应彻底放弃去偏、只追求召回最大化,公平性交给人工事后申诉处理
去偏与召回的张力:过度去偏钝化宗教词,连带漏掉该保护群体内的真实违规,强度要校准
说明宗教词就该一律放行,去偏做得越彻底越好,漏检只是标注口径问题、无需在意
说明该换更大的模型,容量足够大时激进去偏就不会牺牲任何召回,张力自然消失
options_en: It shows debiasing is always harmful; abandon it entirely and just maximize recall, leaving fairness to human appeals afterward.
The debiasing-vs-recall tension: over-debiasing dulls religious terms and drops recall on genuine violations within the protected group, so intensity must be calibrated.
It shows religious terms should just be allowed through; the more thorough the debiasing the better, and misses are merely a labeling-spec issue to ignore.
It shows you need a bigger model; with enough capacity aggressive debiasing sacrifices no recall and the tension disappears.
optionExplanations: 放弃去偏会让 AAVE 等误判卷土重来,而且把公平性甩给事后申诉是被动补救,不是解法。
对;去偏钝化了区分「宗教词」与「针对宗教群体的仇恨」的能力,必须校准强度,兼顾公平与召回。
一律放行会漏掉真实仇恨,方向反了;问题恰恰是去偏过头才漏,不是去偏不够。
加大模型不改变去偏目标本身在压制该群体内真实违规信号,张力是目标冲突,不是容量问题。
optionExplanations_en: Abandoning debiasing brings back AAVE-style misjudgments, and offloading fairness to appeals is passive patching, not a fix.
Correct — debiasing dulls the ability to separate 'religious terms' from 'hate targeting a religious group', so intensity must be calibrated to balance fairness and recall.
Allowing everything through misses real hate — the wrong direction; the problem is over-debiasing causing misses, not too little.
A bigger model doesn't change that the debiasing objective itself suppresses genuine in-group violation signal; the tension is a goal conflict, not capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 去偏做过头,把身份相关信号连同真实违规信号一起抹掉,导致漏检。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Over-debiasing goes too far and erases genuine violation signal along with identity signal, causing misses.

scenario: 团队上线时跑了一次反事实公平测试全部通过,想把它当作一次性验收、之后不再跑。
scenario_en: The team ran counterfactual fairness tests once at launch, all passed, and wants to treat it as a one-time gate.
q: 为什么反事实测试必须持续离线跑?
q_en: Why must counterfactual testing run continuously offline?
why: 语言和俚语在演化,模型会在几个月内漂进新的不公平——今天中性的词过几个月可能被新语境带毒。所以反事实测试要作为持续离线流程反复跑,而不是一次性验收。
why_en: Slang evolves and models drift into unfairness within months, so counterfactual testing must run continuously, not once.
options: 因为一次测试样本不够多,只要第一次多跑几遍取平均,之后就可以永久不再测
因为反事实测试很便宜,顺手多跑几次没坏处,但严格来说一次通过就够了
因为监管要求每季度盖章一次,纯合规动作,与模型公平性是否变化无关
因为语言和俚语在演化,模型会在几个月内漂进新的不公平,必须持续离线反复跑
options_en: Because one test lacks enough samples; just repeat the first run a few times and average, then never test again.
Because counterfactual tests are cheap so a few extra runs don't hurt, but strictly one pass is enough.
Because a regulator requires a quarterly stamp — pure compliance, unrelated to whether the model's fairness changes.
Because language and slang evolve and models drift into unfairness within months, so it must run continuously offline.
optionExplanations: 多跑几遍取平均只降一次性噪声,挡不住分布随时间漂移带来的新偏差。
「便宜就多跑」没抓住根因:必须持续跑是因为公平性会随语言演化而衰退,不是可有可无。
把它当纯合规会错过真实漂移,反事实测试的目的是抓住模型随时间恶化的公平性。
对;俚语和语境在变,今天中性的词几个月后可能带毒,持续离线测试才能及时抓住漂移。
optionExplanations_en: Averaging repeated runs only cuts one-time noise; it can't stop new bias from distribution drift over time.
'Cheap so run more' misses the point: continuous testing is needed because fairness decays as language evolves, not optional.
Treating it as pure compliance misses real drift; the purpose is to catch fairness degrading over time.
Correct — slang and context shift, a neutral word today can turn toxic in months, so continuous offline testing catches the drift in time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上数据分布随时间变化,模型表现(含公平性)逐渐偏离上线时的水平。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model drift is when the live data distribution shifts over time and performance, including fairness, diverges from launch.

scenario: 「drag queens are ruining this country」这句毒性得分 0.82;把「drag queens」换成「politicians」后降到 0.35,句式其它部分完全不变。
scenario_en: 'drag queens are ruining this country' scores 0.82; replacing 'drag queens' with 'politicians' drops it to 0.35, everything else unchanged.
q: 这暴露了哪个公平性概念的失败?
q_en: Which fairness concept does this failure expose?
why: 只替换了身份群体、其余不变,分数却从 0.82 掉到 0.35——这正是反事实公平的失败:决策被身份群体驱动而非内容本身。它不是群体级切片问题,而是逐条内容的身份替换检验。
why_en: Swapping only the identity group flips the score from 0.82 to 0.35, so the decision is driven by identity — a counterfactual fairness failure.
tradeoff: 反事实公平(逐条身份替换、个体级) vs 切片公平(子群平均误差、群体级)
options: 反事实公平失败:仅替换身份群体、其余不变,分数却大幅变化,说明决策被身份驱动
切片评测失败:说明某语言子群的聚合 FPR 超过了全局均值的 2× 上限
校准失败:说明 0.82 这个分数没对齐真实正例率,做温度缩放即可修好
召回失败:说明模型漏检了真实仇恨言论,应整体压低阈值提高召回
options_en: Counterfactual fairness failure: swapping only the identity group flips the score sharply, showing the decision is identity-driven.
Slice evaluation failure: a language subgroup's aggregate FPR exceeded the 2x global-average cap.
Calibration failure: the 0.82 score isn't aligned with the true positive rate, fixable by temperature scaling.
Recall failure: the model missed genuine hate speech, so lower the threshold overall to raise recall.
whenOtherWins: 如果观察到的是「印地语整体 FPR 是英文 3 倍」这种群体级平均差异,而不是同一句只换身份群体的分数跳变,那才该归为切片评测的公平性问题。
optionExplanations: 对;这是经典的身份替换检验:控制其它一切、只换群体,分数剧变即反事实不公平。
切片是群体级平均误差,这里是同一句话的逐条身份替换,粒度不同,不是切片问题。
校准讲分数与概率是否对齐,这里问题是身份替换导致分数跳变,不是刻度失真。
这不是漏检真实仇恨,反而是模型对特定群体过度敏感,压阈值只会加重不公平。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the classic identity-swap test: hold all else fixed, swap only the group, and a big score jump is counterfactual unfairness.
Slice eval is group-level average error; this is a per-item identity swap on one sentence — a different granularity, not a slice issue.
Calibration is about score-vs-probability alignment; here the issue is the identity swap causing a score jump, not a scale distortion.
This isn't missing genuine hate; the model is over-sensitive to a specific group, and lowering the threshold would worsen the unfairness.

termDefinitions.term: identity swap test / 身份替换检验
termDefinitions.meaning: 固定内容其它部分,只替换身份群体词,看模型分数是否变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An identity swap test holds the rest of the content fixed and swaps only the identity-group term to see if the model's score changes.

scenario: 面试官追问:切片评测和反事实公平都在测公平,它们到底差在哪一点?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how slice evaluation and counterfactual fairness actually differ.
q: 两者在「粒度」这一维度上的关键区别是什么?
q_en: On the granularity dimension, what's the key difference?
why: 切片评测是群体级:按维度切子群、比各子群的平均误差(FPR/recall)是否均衡。反事实公平是个体级:固定同一条内容、只换身份特征,看单条决策是否改变。前者查群体分布差异,后者查逐条身份因果。
why_en: Slice eval is group-level average-error balance across subgroups, while counterfactual fairness is individual-level invariance under identity swap.
tradeoff: 切片评测(群体级平均误差均衡) vs 反事实公平(个体级身份替换不变性)
options: 切片是个体级、反事实是群体级,反事实按子群比平均 FPR,切片对单条内容做身份替换
两者粒度相同,只是切片用 recall、反事实用 precision,换个指标而已
切片是群体级(比各子群平均误差),反事实是个体级(同内容换身份看单条决策是否变)
切片只测语言维度、反事实只测宗教维度,区别在覆盖的敏感属性不同,粒度一样
options_en: Slice is individual-level and counterfactual is group-level; counterfactual compares average FPR across subgroups while slice swaps identity on a single item.
Same granularity — slice just uses recall and counterfactual uses precision, only a metric swap.
Slice is group-level (comparing each subgroup's average error) while counterfactual is individual-level (same content, swapped identity, checking if one decision changes).
Slice only tests the language axis and counterfactual only the religion axis; the difference is which sensitive attribute they cover, same granularity.
optionExplanations: 把两者的粒度对调了:切片才是群体级、反事实才是个体级,描述完全反了。
区别不是换指标,而是粒度:一个比群体平均、一个测单条身份替换的不变性。
对;群体级看子群平均误差是否均衡,个体级看同一条内容换身份后决策是否变,互补。
两者都可覆盖多种敏感属性,真正区别在群体级 vs 个体级的粒度,不在覆盖范围。
optionExplanations_en: It swaps the granularities: slice is group-level and counterfactual is individual-level — described backwards.
The difference isn't a metric swap but granularity: one compares group averages, the other tests per-item invariance under identity swap.
Correct — group-level checks subgroup average-error balance, individual-level checks if one item's decision changes under identity swap; they're complementary.
Both can cover multiple sensitive attributes; the real difference is group-level vs individual-level granularity, not coverage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求各子群的平均误差指标(如 FPR)大致均衡,是切片评测的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Group fairness requires subgroups to have roughly equal average-error metrics like FPR, the goal of slice evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求相似个体得到相似决策,反事实公平是其身份替换版本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Individual fairness requires similar individuals to get similar decisions; counterfactual fairness is its identity-swap form.

scenario: 自动升级 + 用户申诉每天涌入上百万条待人工复审,而复审人力有限,当前按先到先得(FIFO)排队。
scenario_en: Auto-escalations plus user appeals bring millions of items/day for human review with limited reviewer capacity, currently served FIFO.
q: 复审队列该怎么组织才能最大化每人工时的伤害削减?
q_en: How should the review queue be organized to maximize harm reduction per reviewer-hour?
why: 把队列优先级建成一个 learning-to-rank 系统,按预期伤害削减给待审项排序,而不是 FIFO。FIFO 把低影响项排在致命高影响项前面,浪费稀缺的复审产能;LTR 让每个人工小时先处理伤害最大的。
why_en: Frame queue prioritization as learning-to-rank that orders items by expected harm reduction, since FIFO wastes scarce reviewer capacity.
tradeoff: LTR 按伤害削减排序(稀缺人力优先处理高危) vs FIFO(先到先得,把致命项排在琐碎项后)
diagram:
flowchart LR E["升级+申诉
百万条/天"] --> R["LTR 排序器"] R --> Q["优先级队列
高伤害在前"] Q --> H["人工复审"]
options: 继续 FIFO,先到先得最公平也最好实现,谁先进队谁先被看,不需要额外模型
把队列优先级建成 learning-to-rank 系统,按预期伤害削减给待审项排序,取代 FIFO
改成后进先出(LIFO),永远先看最新的,越新的内容越重要,老的自然过期不用管
按内容长度排序,长内容信息多、优先复审,短内容一律自动放行以节省人力
options_en: Keep FIFO — first come first served is fairest and simplest, whoever enters first is reviewed first, no extra model needed.
Frame queue prioritization as a learning-to-rank system that orders items by expected harm reduction, replacing FIFO.
Switch to LIFO — always review the newest first since newer content matters more, and old items just expire.
Sort by content length — long items carry more information so review them first, and auto-approve short ones to save effort.
whenOtherWins: 当待审量远小于复审产能、每条都能被及时看到时,排序收益很小,FIFO 的简单和「无偏顺序」反而更省事、更易审计。
optionExplanations: FIFO 简单但盲目,会让一条 10 万浏览的边界仇恨排在一条 10 浏览垃圾之后,浪费产能。
对;LTR 学着按伤害削减排序,把稀缺人工小时先投给最致命/最具影响的项,收益最大。
LIFO 让积压的老违规永远排不上,反而制造大量长期漏检,更差。
长度和伤害无关,按长度排会漏掉短小但极危险的内容,是个无关代理指标。
optionExplanations_en: FIFO is simple but blind, putting a 100K-view borderline hate item behind a 10-view spam and wasting capacity.
Correct — LTR learns to order by harm reduction, spending scarce reviewer-hours on the most lethal/impactful items first for maximum payoff.
LIFO leaves backlogged old violations forever unreviewed, creating large long-term misses — worse.
Length is unrelated to harm; sorting by it misses short but highly dangerous content — an irrelevant proxy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先到先得的队列顺序,不区分待审项的伤害或影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO (First In First Out) serves items in arrival order, ignoring each item's harm or impact.

termDefinitions.term: harm reduction per reviewer-hour / 每人工时伤害削减
termDefinitions.meaning: 每投入一个复审人工小时所能消除的预期伤害,是队列优化的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Harm reduction per reviewer-hour is the expected harm removed per hour of review, the queue's optimization objective.

scenario: 你要给复审队列的 LTR 排序器设计打分信号,需要覆盖伤害和模型改进两方面。
scenario_en: You're designing the scoring signals for the review-queue LTR ranker, covering both harm and model improvement.
q: 队列排序应综合哪些信号?(多选)
q_en: Which signals should the queue ranking combine? (multiple)
why: 四个信号:违规严重度(儿童安全>仇恨>垃圾)、模型不确定性(最没把握的项标注价值最高)、内容传播度(高浏览/高转发优先)、时效性(直播/热点衰减快要快审)。前两个偏模型改进,后两个偏伤害削减。
why_en: Combine violation severity, model uncertainty, content virality, and time sensitivity — the four signals spanning harm reduction and model improvement.
options: 违规严重度(儿童安全 > 仇恨言论 > 垃圾,与代价层级一致)
模型不确定性(最没把握的项标注后信息量最大)
内容传播度(高浏览/高转发/高触达优先)
时效性(直播/热点类违规衰减快,需要更快周转)
options_en: Violation severity (child safety > hate speech > spam, matching the cost hierarchy).
Model uncertainty (least-confident items yield the most informative labels).
Content virality (high views/shares/reach get priority).
Time sensitivity (live/trending violations decay fast and need faster turnaround).
optionExplanations: 对;严重度直接对齐政策代价层级,把复审优先投给伤害最大的类别。
对;不确定性高的项标注后对模型提升最大,喂养主动学习飞轮。
对;高传播内容的每分钟伤害更大,优先审能削掉更多总伤害。
对;直播/热点的违规窗口短,晚审等于没审,时效性推动更快周转。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — severity aligns with the policy cost hierarchy, sending review to the most harmful categories first.
Correct — labeling high-uncertainty items improves the model most, feeding the active-learning flywheel.
Correct — viral content harms more per minute, so reviewing it first removes more total harm.
Correct — live/trending violations have short windows, so late review is no review; time sensitivity drives faster turnaround.

termDefinitions.term: model uncertainty / 模型不确定性
termDefinitions.meaning: 模型对某项判定的置信度低;这类项人工标注后信息量最大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model uncertainty is low confidence on an item; labeling such items yields the most information for the model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容的浏览量、转发速度、触达范围,衡量其潜在影响面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content virality is an item's views, share velocity, and reach, measuring its potential impact.

scenario: 复审队列除了削减伤害,还想顺便产出对模型训练最有价值的标注。
scenario_en: Beyond cutting harm, the review queue should also produce the labels most valuable for training.
q: 为什么要把「模型最没把握的项」优先送人工?
q_en: Why prioritize the items the model is least confident about for human review?
why: 最没把握的项(置信度接近阈值)标注后信息量最大,人工判定正好补上模型的盲区,形成主动学习飞轮:审这些项既产出标签又直接提升下一版模型。代价是这类项当下伤害未必最高,要和严重度/传播度加权平衡。
why_en: Least-confident items yield the most informative labels, so reviewing them feeds an active-learning flywheel that improves the next model.
tradeoff: 优先审不确定项(标注信息量大、喂养飞轮) vs 优先审高严重度/高传播(当下削减伤害最多)
diagram:
flowchart LR
  U["最不确定的项"] --> H["人工判定"]
  H --> L["高信息量标签"]
  L --> M["更好的模型"]
  M --> U
options: 因为不确定的项一定是最危险的,置信度低就等于伤害大,所以优先审
因为不确定的项数量最少,先清掉能最快清空队列、降低积压
因为最没把握的项标注后信息量最大,补模型盲区、喂养主动学习飞轮,持续提升下一版模型
因为高置信度项已经准了、无需人看,把它们全部自动执行就能省下所有人力
options_en: Because uncertain items are always the most dangerous — low confidence equals high harm, so review them first.
Because uncertain items are the fewest, so clearing them first empties the queue fastest and cuts backlog.
Because least-confident items give the most informative labels, filling model blind spots and feeding an active-learning flywheel that improves the next model.
Because high-confidence items are already accurate and need no human, so auto-executing all of them saves all the manpower.
optionExplanations: 不确定 ≠ 高危;有些不确定项其实是低伤害的模糊垃圾,不能把两者划等号。
不确定项数量并不天然最少,而且「清空队列」不是优先级目标,伤害削减和模型提升才是。
对;低置信项贴着决策边界,人工标注最能纠偏,形成审→标→更好模型→再审的飞轮。
高置信也可能校准不准而误判,全自动执行会放大系统性错误,不能因此撤掉全部人工。
optionExplanations_en: Uncertain is not high-risk; some uncertain items are low-harm ambiguous spam, so you can't equate the two.
Uncertain items aren't inherently fewest, and 'emptying the queue' isn't the objective — harm reduction and model improvement are.
Correct — low-confidence items sit on the decision boundary where labels correct the most, forming a review-to-label-to-better-model flywheel.
High confidence can still be miscalibrated and wrong; full auto-execution amplifies systematic errors, so you can't drop all human review.

termDefinitions.meaning: 优先让人标注模型最不确定的样本,用最少标注量最快提升模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Active learning prioritizes human labeling of the model's most uncertain samples to improve it fastest with the fewest labels.

scenario: 队列里有两条同样置信度、同样是边界仇恨言论:A 已 10 万浏览且还在快速转发,B 只有 10 浏览。复审产能有限,只能先看一条。
scenario_en: Two same-confidence borderline hate items sit in the queue: A has 100K views and is spreading fast, B has 10 views. Capacity lets you review only one first.
q: 应该先审哪条、依据什么信号?
q_en: Which do you review first, and by which signal?
why: 先审 A:传播度信号(浏览量、转发速度、触达)决定潜在伤害面。10 万浏览且在扩散的边界项每分钟造成的伤害远大于 10 浏览的,优先审 A 能在单位人工时削减最多伤害。
why_en: Review A first — content virality (views, share velocity, reach) determines potential harm, and a spreading 100K-view item harms far more than a 10-view one.
tradeoff: 按传播度优先(先审高触达、削减总伤害) vs 忽略传播度(把高扩散项和冷门项同等对待)
options: 先审 A:传播度信号(浏览/转发/触达)决定伤害面,10 万浏览且在扩散的项每分钟伤害远大于 10 浏览
先审 B:浏览少说明还没扩散、更容易悄悄处理掉,先清冷门项能避免引起公众注意
无所谓先审哪条:两条置信度相同,传播度与复审优先级无关,按到达顺序处理即可
两条都先不审:等 A 的浏览自然回落再说,热度过去伤害就消失了,不必占用人力
options_en: Review A first: virality (views/shares/reach) sets the harm surface, and a spreading 100K-view item harms far more per minute than a 10-view one.
Review B first: few views means it hasn't spread and is easier to quietly remove, and clearing cold items avoids drawing public attention.
Doesn't matter which first: same confidence, and virality is irrelevant to review priority, so process in arrival order.
Review neither yet: wait for A's views to fall, since once the hype passes the harm disappears and no manpower is needed.
whenOtherWins: 若 B 属于更高严重度类别(如儿童安全)而 A 只是低严重度边界项,则严重度信号压过传播度,应先审 B——传播度只是加权信号之一。
optionExplanations: 对;传播度直接换算成伤害面,先审高扩散项能在有限人力下削掉最多总伤害。
先审冷门项是本末倒置,任由高扩散仇恨继续传播,伤害在你处理 B 时持续累积。
同置信度下传播度恰恰是关键区分信号,按到达顺序等于放弃优先级、退回 FIFO。
等热度回落=放任伤害发生,违规内容在传播期已造成实际危害,不能靠拖延消解。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — virality maps to harm surface, so reviewing the high-spread item first removes the most total harm under limited capacity.
Reviewing the cold item first is backwards, letting high-spread hate keep spreading and accruing harm while you handle B.
At equal confidence, virality is exactly the distinguishing signal; arrival order abandons prioritization and reverts to FIFO.
Waiting for hype to fall lets harm happen; violating content already causes real damage during spread, not resolvable by delay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间内的转发/传播增速,衡量内容正在扩散得多快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Share velocity is the rate of reshares per unit time, measuring how fast content is spreading.

scenario: 队列里同时有一条直播中的热点事件违规和一条三天前的普通帖违规,两者严重度相近。
scenario_en: The queue holds a live trending-event violation and a three-day-old regular-post violation of similar severity.
q: 时效性信号为什么把直播/热点类往前排?
q_en: Why does the time-sensitivity signal push live/trending items forward?
why: 直播/热点类违规衰减快:观众和影响集中在很短的窗口内,晚几分钟审就等于错过了大部分伤害。所以时效性信号要求这类项更快周转,而不是和长尾旧帖同等排队。
why_en: Live/trending violations decay fast, so their harm is concentrated in a short window and they need faster turnaround than old posts.
options: 因为直播内容一定比旧帖更严重,时效性其实就是严重度的另一种叫法
因为直播/热点违规衰减快、伤害集中在很短窗口,晚审就错过大部分伤害,需更快周转
因为直播数据量大、占存储多,先审掉能尽快释放存储资源、降低成本
因为旧帖已被更多人举报、证据更充分,可以放后面慢慢处理,先清证据不足的直播
options_en: Because live content is always more severe than old posts — time sensitivity is just another name for severity.
Because live/trending violations decay fast with harm concentrated in a short window, so late review misses most of the harm and they need faster turnaround.
Because live streams are large and use lots of storage, so clearing them first frees storage and cuts cost.
Because old posts already have more reports and stronger evidence, so handle them later and clear the evidence-thin live items first.
optionExplanations: 时效性和严重度是两个独立信号:一条低严重度的热点项也可能因窗口短而需要快审,不能混为一谈。
对;时效性衡量的是伤害窗口长短,窗口短就必须快周转,否则审完伤害已经发生完了。
存储成本和复审优先级无关,这是把运维成本和伤害削减目标混淆了。
举报多寡不是排序依据,拖延处理短窗口的直播违规恰恰会错过它的伤害高峰。
optionExplanations_en: Time sensitivity and severity are independent signals; a low-severity trending item may still need fast review due to a short window, so don't conflate them.
Correct — time sensitivity measures the harm window's length; a short window demands fast turnaround or the harm is already done by review time.
Storage cost is unrelated to review priority — conflating ops cost with the harm-reduction objective.
Report count isn't the ordering basis, and delaying a short-window live violation precisely misses its harm peak.

termDefinitions.meaning: 违规内容的伤害窗口长短;窗口短(如直播)的项需要更快复审周转。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time sensitivity is how short a violation's harm window is; short-window items like live streams need faster review turnaround.

scenario: 你要训练复审队列的 LTR 排序器,得先想清楚标签和特征分别是什么。
scenario_en: To train the review-queue LTR ranker, you must define its labels and features.
q: 这个 LTR 系统的标签和特征分别是什么?
q_en: What are the labels and features of this LTR system?
why: 标签 = 复审员对历史待审项判定的严重度(人工给出的真值);特征 = 四个信号(严重度预测、模型不确定性、传播度、时效性)加上内容年龄、作者历史。排序器学着把「预计伤害削减大」的项排前面。
why_en: Labels are reviewer-determined severity on historical items, and features are the four signals plus content age and author history.
options: 标签=内容浏览量,特征=复审员是谁;学着把浏览高的排前面
标签=复审员对历史项判定的严重度;特征=四信号(严重度/不确定性/传播度/时效)+内容年龄+作者历史
标签=模型自己的置信分,特征=文本长度和语言;不需要人工标注,自监督即可
标签=该项最终是否被删,特征=删除耗时;学着预测处理时长以调度人力
options_en: Labels = content view count, features = which reviewer handled it; learn to rank high-view items first.
Labels = reviewer-determined severity on historical items; features = the four signals (severity/uncertainty/virality/time) plus content age and author history.
Labels = the model's own confidence score, features = text length and language; no human labels needed, self-supervised suffices.
Labels = whether the item was ultimately removed, features = removal latency; learn to predict handling time to schedule staff.
optionExplanations: 浏览量是特征之一(传播度),不是标签;标签得是人工判定的严重度真值。
对;人工复审给出的严重度是监督信号,四信号+内容年龄+作者历史构成特征,学排序。
拿模型自己的置信分当标签会自我强化偏差,LTR 要学的是人工判定的伤害,不是模型自评。
「是否被删」太粗且滞后,预测处理时长也不是队列优先级目标——目标是伤害削减排序。
optionExplanations_en: View count is a feature (virality), not a label; the label must be human-determined severity ground truth.
Correct — reviewer-determined severity is the supervision signal, with the four signals plus content age and author history as features for ranking.
Using the model's own confidence as the label self-reinforces bias; LTR should learn human-judged harm, not model self-assessment.
'Whether removed' is coarse and lagging, and predicting handling time isn't the queue objective — the objective is ranking by harm reduction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 作者过往的违规记录,作为复审排序的一个特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Author history is the author's past violation record, used as a feature in review ranking.

scenario: 平台刚出现一种全新违规类型,模型对它普遍没把握;而队列的 LTR 得同时兼顾「当下削减伤害」和「提升模型」。
scenario_en: A brand-new violation type appears with the model broadly unsure about it, while the queue's LTR must balance cutting harm now and improving the model.
q: 此刻该怎么调排序权重?
q_en: How should you tune the ranking weights right now?
why: 用可调权重把伤害削减(严重度×传播度)和模型改进(按不确定性)线性组合。面对新违规类型、模型表现差时,临时调高不确定性权重多收这类标注;等危机爆发时再让严重度/传播度主导。权重随处境切换,不是固定的。
why_en: Use tunable weights over harm reduction and model improvement, raising the uncertainty weight when the model underperforms on a new type.
tradeoff: 临时提高不确定性权重(快速补标新类型、改进模型) vs 维持严重度/传播度主导(优先削减当下伤害)
options: 把不确定性权重砍到 0、只按严重度×传播度排,新类型交给模型自己慢慢适应即可
临时调高不确定性权重、多收新类型的高信息标注以改进模型;危机爆发时再让严重度/传播度主导
把所有权重永久固定成相等,任何情况都不调,靠稳定性避免运营复杂度
直接停用 LTR、退回 FIFO,等模型学会新类型再重新启用排序器
options_en: Cut the uncertainty weight to 0 and rank only by severity times virality, letting the model slowly adapt to the new type on its own.
Temporarily raise the uncertainty weight to collect more high-information labels on the new type to improve the model; during a crisis let severity/virality dominate.
Fix all weights permanently equal and never tune them, using stability to avoid operational complexity.
Disable LTR and revert to FIFO until the model learns the new type, then re-enable the ranker.
whenOtherWins: 如果此刻正处于某类违规的危机激增(如一起线下事件引爆的大规模仇恨),就该把权重反过来让严重度/传播度主导,先扑灭当下伤害,把补标新类型的事往后放。
optionExplanations: 砍掉不确定性权重就断了主动学习,新类型永远补不上标注,模型对它一直没把握。
对;权重可调正是为了顺应处境:新类型缺数据时抬不确定性权重,危机时抬严重度/传播度。
永久固定权重放弃了这套设计的灵活性,无法在「补模型」和「灭火」间动态切换。
退回 FIFO 会同时丢掉伤害排序和主动学习,比调权重差得多,是过度反应。
optionExplanations_en: Zeroing the uncertainty weight cuts off active learning, so the new type never gets labels and the model stays unsure about it.
Correct — tunable weights exist to adapt: raise the uncertainty weight when a new type lacks data, raise severity/virality during a crisis.
Permanently fixed weights abandon the design's flexibility and can't switch dynamically between improving the model and firefighting.
Reverting to FIFO loses both harm ordering and active learning at once — far worse than tuning weights, an overreaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个排序信号线性组合时每个信号的系数,可按处境上下调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tunable weights are the coefficients combining ranking signals linearly, adjustable up or down by situation.

scenario: 面试里你想展示 Staff 级的系统思维,而不只是把审核当成一个分类器。
scenario_en: In the interview you want to show Staff-level systems thinking, not just treat moderation as one classifier.
q: 关于复审队列,哪个表述最体现 Staff 级洞察?
q_en: Which statement best shows Staff-level insight about the review queue?
why: 把复审队列当作与违规分类器相互独立的另一个 ML 系统(它有自己的标签、特征、目标和飞轮),是 Staff 级系统思维。junior 往往只优化分类器,忽视了「谁先被人看」本身就是一个可优化、可训练的排序问题。
why_en: Framing the review queue as its own ML system, separate from the violation classifier, is the Staff-level systems-thinking insight.
options: 把复审队列当作与违规分类器相互独立的另一个 ML 系统,有自己的标签/特征/目标和飞轮
复审队列只是分类器的一个输出缓冲区,不含任何机器学习,按时间戳排队即可
复审队列应和分类器共用同一个模型和同一套标签,合并成一个端到端网络最省事
复审队列的唯一价值是限流,防止人工被冲垮,和排序、模型改进都没有关系
options_en: Frame the review queue as its own ML system, separate from the violation classifier, with its own labels/features/objective and flywheel.
The review queue is just an output buffer of the classifier with no machine learning, ordered by timestamp.
The review queue should share one model and one label set with the classifier, merged into a single end-to-end network for simplicity.
The review queue's only value is rate-limiting to keep reviewers from being overwhelmed, unrelated to ranking or model improvement.
optionExplanations: 对;队列有独立的优化目标(每人工时伤害削减)和训练数据,把它当独立 ML 系统正是 Staff 级视角。
把它当纯缓冲区就退回 FIFO,丢掉了按伤害削减排序这个可训练的优化问题。
队列的标签(复审员严重度)和目标(排序伤害)与分类器不同,强行合并会互相拖累、目标错配。
限流只是副作用;队列的核心价值是优先级排序和喂养主动学习,不止防冲垮。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the queue has its own objective (harm reduction per reviewer-hour) and training data, so treating it as a separate ML system is the Staff-level view.
Treating it as a pure buffer reverts to FIFO and drops the trainable optimization of ranking by harm reduction.
The queue's labels (reviewer severity) and objective (ranking harm) differ from the classifier's; forcing a merge causes mutual drag and goal misalignment.
Rate-limiting is a side effect; the queue's core value is prioritization and feeding active learning, not just avoiding overload.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个子模块(如复审队列)识别为有独立目标和数据的完整系统,而非附属组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Systems thinking recognizes a submodule like the review queue as a full system with its own objective and data, not a mere appendage.

scenario: 成本敏感阈值假设分类器的分数就是真实概率,校准正是保证这一点。
scenario_en: Cost-sensitive thresholds assume the classifier's score is the true probability, which calibration ensures.
q: 补全校准的定义与失校的后果:
q_en: Complete the definition of calibration and the effect of miscalibration:
text: 校准的含义是:模型在某分数段输出的置信度应等于该段的真实{{正例率}};若它在 0.7 处输出但真实正例率只有 0.5,则按分数选阈值就{{不可靠}},因为分数与真实概率{{脱节}}。
text_en: Calibration means the model's confidence at a score band should equal the true {{positive rate}} there; if it outputs 0.7 but the true rate is 0.5, choosing thresholds by score is {{unreliable}} because score and true probability are {{decoupled}}.
why: 校准把「分数」和「真实概率」绑在一起,是成本敏感阈值成立的前提;失校时代价比推出的阈值会落在错误的召回点上。它的下游用途:只有校准好,per-category 阈值和 per-slice 阈值调整才可信。
why_en: Calibration ties score to true probability, the prerequisite for cost-sensitive and per-slice thresholds to be trustworthy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某分数段样本中真实为违规的比例;校准要求它等于模型输出的置信度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The positive rate is the fraction of items in a score band that are truly violating; calibration requires it to equal the model's confidence.

q: 把审核评测从 junior 到 Staff 的成熟度阶梯按四支柱顺序排列:
q_en: Order the moderation-evaluation maturity ladder from junior to Staff along the four pillars:
steps: 沿语言/社区等切片独立算 P/R/F1/FPR,并设最大差异阈值
只报一个聚合 F1 就停 = junior 水平,L5+ 才往下拆
把人工复审队列当作独立的 learning-to-rank 系统排优先级
按政策代价比给每个违规类别单独定阈值(成本敏感)
对个体做反事实公平测试并持续离线跑
why: 阶梯:报单一 F1 就停=junior→支柱一成本敏感阈值→支柱二切片评测→支柱三反事实公平→支柱四 LTR 队列。四支柱把系统从「平均能用」推到「公平可用」,且应在被问公平性前主动提出。
why_en: From stopping at one F1 (junior) up through cost-sensitive thresholds, slice eval, counterfactual fairness, and the LTR queue, moving from 'works on average' to 'works equitably'.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从只报聚合指标到主动做四支柱评测的能力进阶,对应 junior→L5→Staff。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The maturity ladder is the progression from reporting only aggregate metrics to proactively running the four evaluation pillars, junior to Staff.
